subject: music
topicDisplay: Areas Of Inquiry Music Technology In The Electronic And Digital Age
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Swing-era big bands such as Count Basie's typically organised their players into which sectional layout?
questions.explain: Big bands are built around a saxophone section, a brass section and a rhythm section.

questions.q: Debussy is most closely associated with which musical movement?
questions.explain: Debussy is the leading figure of musical Impressionism, using whole-tone scales and coloured harmonies.

questions.q: The Argentine 'tango' is most associated with which instrument providing its characteristic sound?
questions.explain: The bandoneón, a button accordion, gives the tango its distinctive timbre.

questions.q: 'Fusion' music is best defined as...?
options: A style that blends elements of two or more distinct traditions or genres
Music performed only on acoustic instruments
questions.explain: Fusion combines features of two or more traditions or genres, such as jazz-rock or Indian-Western fusion.

questions.q: An atonal passage is best characterised by which feature?
options: A clear tonic and dominant relationship
Strict adherence to a major scale
The absence of a tonal centre or key
questions.explain: Atonality avoids any sense of a key or tonal centre, abandoning functional harmony.

questions.q: The technique of word-painting describes which practice?
options: Music that reflects the literal meaning of the text
Painting visual scenery for an opera
questions.explain: Word-painting depicts the meaning of the words in the music, such as rising lines on the word 'ascend'.

questions.q: Steve Reich is a leading composer of which 20th-century style?
questions.explain: Reich is a key minimalist, known for phasing and repetitive interlocking patterns.

questions.q: In Indian classical music the term 'bol' refers to...?
options: Mnemonic syllables used to represent and recite drum strokes or rhythms
questions.explain: Bols are spoken mnemonic syllables representing tabla strokes and rhythmic patterns.

questions.q: A 'walking bass' line in jazz is most characterised by which feature?
options: A steady stream of crotchets outlining the chords, usually one note per beat
A sustained pedal note held under the harmony
questions.explain: A walking bass moves in even crotchets, typically one note per beat, threading through the chord tones to drive the harmony forward.

questions.q: A melodic sequence is best described as which?
options: The repetition of a melodic pattern at a different pitch level
The simultaneous sounding of two melodies
A note held against changing harmony
The inversion of a melodic line
questions.explain: A sequence repeats a melodic (or harmonic) idea successively higher or lower in pitch.

questions.q: In jazz performance, 'swung' quavers are most accurately understood as pairs of quavers played roughly as...?
options: A triplet feel, long-short (approximately quarter-eighth of a triplet)
A short-long anticipation on every beat
questions.explain: Swung quavers approximate a triplet division, giving a long-short 'lilt' to each pair.

questions.q: An Alberti bass is which kind of accompaniment figure?
options: A broken-chord pattern in the left hand of keyboard music
questions.explain: The Alberti bass breaks a chord into a steady low-high-middle-high arpeggiated pattern, common in the Classical era.

questions.q: In film music, a 'leitmotif' is...?
options: A sudden silence used for dramatic effect
A recurring musical theme associated with a particular character, place or idea
A piece of source music heard within the scene
questions.explain: A leitmotif is a recurring theme linked to a specific character, place or idea, a technique developed by Wagner and used widely in film.

questions.q: A recitative in Baroque opera primarily serves which function?
options: To display vocal virtuosity in an aria
To advance the plot through speech-like singing
questions.explain: Recitative uses a free, speech-like vocal style to carry the narrative between arias.

questions.q: Neoclassicism in the 20th century is characterised by which approach?
options: Reviving Classical and Baroque forms with modern harmony
questions.explain: Neoclassicism, associated with Stravinsky, revisits older forms and clarity while applying a modern harmonic language.

questions.q: The minuet and trio movement of a Classical symphony is typically in which metre?
questions.explain: The minuet, derived from a dance, is in a moderate triple metre.

questions.q: The standard twelve-bar blues progression in its basic form follows which sequence of chords (in bars)?
questions.explain: The classic twelve-bar blues uses four bars of I, two of IV returning to I, then V-IV-I across the final four bars.

questions.q: Programme music is best defined as which?
options: Music written from a printed programme of events
Instrumental music that depicts a narrative or extra-musical idea
questions.explain: Programme music tells a story or evokes images or ideas beyond the music itself, common in the Romantic era.

questions.q: Sonata form consists of which three main sections?
questions.explain: Sonata form unfolds in exposition, development and recapitulation, often with an introduction and coda.

questions.q: A tonic pedal is best described as which device?
options: A modulation to the tonic minor
A melodic ornament on the tonic
A rapid alternation of tonic and dominant
A sustained tonic note held while harmonies change above it
questions.explain: A pedal is a sustained or repeated note, the tonic pedal holding the tonic while other parts move through changing harmonies.

questions.q: Motown, the Detroit-based label of the 1960s, is associated with which of the following hallmarks?
options: Free improvisation with no fixed form
A polished soul-pop sound with the 'Funk Brothers' house band, tambourine back-beats and call-and-response vocals
questions.explain: Motown produced a slick soul-pop sound built on a house band, back-beat percussion and gospel-derived call-and-response vocals.

questions.q: A fugue opens with which compositional procedure?
options: A subject stated alone then imitated by successive voices
questions.explain: A fugue begins with a subject announced in one voice, answered imitatively by entering voices.

questions.q: A retardation differs from a suspension in which way?
options: It resolves upward by step rather than downward
questions.explain: A retardation is a suspended note that resolves upward by step, whereas a suspension resolves downward.

questions.q: The typical jazz 'rhythm section' that accompanies soloists usually comprises which combination?
options: Piano (or guitar), double bass and drums
questions.explain: The rhythm section conventionally consists of a chordal instrument (piano/guitar), bass and drums.

questions.q: In song structure terminology, a 'bridge' (or 'middle eight') typically functions to...?
options: Provide contrast in melody/harmony before returning to the chorus or verse
State the main hook for the first time
End the song with a fade-out
questions.explain: The bridge offers contrasting material that breaks up verse-chorus repetition before a return.

questions.q: Brahms is generally regarded as a Romantic composer who upheld which trait?
options: Classical formal structures within a Romantic idiom
questions.explain: Brahms combined Romantic expression with Classical forms such as the symphony and sonata, in the absolute-music tradition.

questions.q: In a Classical concerto first movement, the cadenza traditionally occurs at which point?
options: At the very opening before the orchestra plays
Near the end, over a tonic six-four before the final tutti
In the middle of the development only
questions.explain: The cadenza, a virtuosic solo passage, typically falls near the movement's end on a cadential six-four leading to the closing tutti.

questions.q: The 'tabla' is...?
options: A pair of hand drums of different sizes and pitches
questions.explain: The tabla is a pair of tuned hand drums central to North Indian rhythmic accompaniment.

questions.q: In music technology, 'sampling' is best described as...?
options: Recording in a single continuous take
Taking a portion of an existing sound recording and reusing it within a new piece
questions.explain: Sampling reuses a fragment of an existing recording as material within a new track.

questions.q: The studio effect 'reverb' is used to...?
options: Shift the pitch of a vocal up an octave
Speed up the tempo of a track
Simulate the natural reflections of a sound in a space, adding sense of depth/ambience
questions.explain: Reverb recreates the reflections of a physical space, adding depth and ambience to a sound.
